label: position 2 right after q as the 2nd original token
explanation: Fires at step t=2 of the original phase whenever the second original token (input at t=1) was q, i.e. the step after reading q in position 1, regardless of the current token or L. Dev P=1.00, R=0.998. Magnitude seems to depend on the first token: all top examples (activation 1.0) start with b, and low-quartile examples start with i/d/h. That comes from looking at examples and was not tested systematically. It does not fire for q at other positions or at the delimiter, and it essentially never fires in the copy phase (the copy-phase replay of q at position 1 does not trigger it). The only misses are weak activations at t=3 when q is repeated in positions 1 and 2.

issues: Test split: P=1.000, R=0.998, F1=0.999, mass recall 0.9996, zero false positives. The only misses are 38 weak steps (0.0% of activation mass), all at t=3 in sequences starting X q q, mostly j q q (0.69) and r q q (0.31). The explanation already describes these, so they don't count as an unexplained class.

Phase and position claims check out on dev: no activity at the delimiter, 1 active step in the copy phase out of 2.73M, and 16746 of 16781 active steps at t=2. Firing does not depend on the current token (each in_tok has about the same rate) or on L, apart from the expected per-step dilution.

The magnitude claim is weak and untested. All top examples (activation 1.0) start 'b q' but also have current token 't' ('b q t'), so the peak may depend on both the first and the current token, not just the first. The profile shows activation mass spread evenly across first tokens. Treat this as an anecdote, not a finding. It doesn't affect the firing predicate.
